Task: Match a bare ten-digit phone number with no separators.

Write a pattern that matches exactly the strings that should match.

Must match:
  '0000000000'
Must not match:

turns.thinking: Using '+' would accept any length of digit run, which the fixed length rules out. Pattern: \d{10}

Task: Now insert hyphens so 5551234567 becomes 555-123-4567.

Write a pattern and replacement that produce the requested output.

Examples (input -> output):
  '1234567890' -> '123-456-7890'
turns.thinking: Formatting inserts separators without reordering, so each of the three fields needs its own group. Pattern: \b(\d{3})(\d{3})(\d{4})\b with replacement \1-\2-\3

turns.instruction: Some numbers carry a +1 country code. Keep the +1 where present and still format the rest as 555-123-4567.

turns.thinking: Python substitutes an unmatched optional group as empty, so the same replacement handles both the prefixed and bare forms. Pattern: (\+1)?(\d{3})(\d{3})(\d{4}) with replacement \1\2-\3-\4
